Loading libraries

This chunk loads all the necessary R packages and resources for the downstream single-cell and pseudobulk analyses.

  • scater: used for visualization and processing of single-cell data.
  • RUVSeq: provides functions for normalization using control genes (RUV normalization).
  • darioscripts: a custom helper package with user-defined functions.
  • DT: used to generate interactive HTML tables.
  • ggpubr and ggrepel: utilities to produce clean ggplot-based visualizations with non-overlapping text labels.
  • utils.R: a script with additional helper functions, sourced from the ../R/ directory.
  • The color palette used for plotting (subcluster.color) is loaded from a pre-saved .RData file and assigned to palette.

Some libraries and scripts are commented out, likely because they are either not currently needed or replaced by custom implementations.

Code 
library(scater)
library(ggpubr)
library(RUVSeq)
library(darioscripts)
library(DT)
library(ggrepel)
source("../R/utils.R")
load("~/Downloads/multiome_data/data/MultiomeAllenColorLabel.RData")
palette <- subcluster.color

Visualization for WT Samples

This chunk performs dimensionality reduction and visualization for wild-type (WT) and sleep-deprived (SD) samples from a filtered single-cell RNA-seq dataset.

  • The SingleCellExperiment object list scelist is first read from a file containing RNA-only data with doublets removed.
  • Only WT and SD samples are selected using a regex filter.
  • Dimensionality reduction is computed using PCA, followed by tSNE and UMAP, which are embedded into the scelistwt objects.
  • Sample names containing _WT are renamed to _HC (likely to represent healthy controls).
  • For each sample, two plots are created: a tSNE and a UMAP, colored by annotated cell labels.
  • These plots are arranged side-by-side and labeled with the sample name using ggpubr.

This step is useful for visually inspecting clustering patterns and checking label separability across conditions.

Code 
scelist <- readRDS("~/Downloads/multiome_data/data/scelist_SR_dbl_signacfilt_dimred_noATAC_doublrm.RDS")
scelists3 <- scelist[grep("_S3", names(scelist))]
rm(scelist)

set.seed(3)
scelists3 <- lapply(scelists3, runTSNE, dimred="PCA")
scelists3 <- lapply(scelists3, runUMAP, dimred="PCA")
names(scelists3) <- gsub("_S3$", "_S3HC", names(scelists3))
lapply(seq_along(scelists3), function(i)
{
    sce <- scelists3[[i]]
    ts <- plotReducedDim(sce, dimred="TSNE", colour_by="labels", point_size=1)+scale_color_manual(values=palette)+theme_bw()
    um <- plotReducedDim(sce, dimred="UMAP", colour_by="labels", point_size=1)+scale_color_manual(values=palette)+theme_bw()
    gga <- ggarrange(plotlist=list(ts, um), common.legend=TRUE)
    annotate_figure(gga, top=ggpubr::text_grob(names(scelists3)[i], 
    color = "black", face = "bold", size = 14))
})

Load and Annotate Pseudobulk Data (All Cell Types)

In this section, we load pseudobulk gene expression data and perform key preprocessing steps:

  • The multiome object, a SingleCellExperiment storing pseudobulk counts, is loaded from disk.
  • Each sample is annotated with a superclass label: either “Non Neuronal”, “Neuronal - Glutamatergic”, or “Neuronal - Gabaergic” based on known cell types.
  • We load a list of known negative control genes (used later in RUV normalization) and assign a subset as a test set (10% of them).
  • Similarly, positive control genes are loaded and flagged.
  • We then restrict the data to only Shank3 DeltaC (S3) samples and remove cell types not detected in all samples (fewer than 6 replicates).
  • Library size normalization and log-normalization are performed.
  • Finally, we compute and plot MDS and PCA embeddings to assess clustering across cell types and conditions.
Code 
multiome <- readRDS("~/Downloads/multiome_data/data/GEX_pseudo_2023.RDS") # pseudobulk

multiome$superclass <- "Non Neuronal"
multiome$superclass[multiome$label %in% c("CA1", "CA1-do","CA1-ProS", "CA2", "CA3", "SUB-ProS", "DG")] <- "Neuronal - Glutamatergic"
multiome$superclass[multiome$label %in% c("Lamp5", "Sncg", "Vip", "Serpinf1",
                                          "Ntng1", "Pvalb", "Sst", "Sst-Chodl")] <-
    "Neuronal - Gabaergic"
nc <- readRDS("~/Downloads/multiome_data/ctrls/SD_neg_ctrl.RDS")
dim(nc)
[1] 4033    2
Code 
rowData(multiome)$negctl <- FALSE
rowData(multiome)$negctl[rownames(multiome) %in% nc$symbol] <- TRUE

set.seed(3)
idxsamp <- sample(seq_along(nc$ensembl_id), round((dim(nc)[1]*10)/100))
nctest <- nc[idxsamp,]
nc <- nc[-idxsamp,]
rowData(multiome)$negctl <- FALSE
rowData(multiome)$negctl[rownames(multiome) %in% nc$symbol] <- TRUE
rowData(multiome)$negctltest <- FALSE
rowData(multiome)$negctltest[rownames(multiome) %in% nctest$symbol] <- TRUE

newps <- read.table("~/Downloads/multiome_data/ctrls/111022_Positive_Controls_from_BMC_Genomics_AddFile2.txt", header=TRUE)
newpshits <- newps
rowData(multiome)$posctl <- FALSE
rowData(multiome)$posctl[rownames(multiome) %in% newps$Gene_Name] <- TRUE

newpshits$kept <- FALSE
newpshits$kept[which(newpshits$Gene_Name %in% rownames(multiome))] <- TRUE

multiome$condition[multiome$condition=="CTRL"] <- "HC"
multiomes3 <- multiome[,multiome$genotype=="S3"]
noct <- names(which(table(multiomes3$label)<6))
multiomes3 <- multiomes3[,-which(multiomes3$labels %in% noct)]
multiomes3 <- computeLibraryFactors(multiomes3)
multiomes3 <- logNormCounts(multiomes3)
multiomes3 <- runMDS(multiomes3)
mdal <- scater::plotMDS(multiomes3, color_by="labels", shape_by="condition", point_alpha=1)+scale_color_manual(values=palette)+theme_bw()
pcal <- plotPCA(multiomes3, color_by="labels", shape_by="condition", point_alpha=1)+scale_color_manual(values=palette)+theme_bw()
ggarrange(plotlist=list(mdal, pcal), common.legend=TRUE)

Annotate Genes with External Feature Information

In this step, gene-level metadata is added to the rowData of the multiomes3 object. These annotations include:

  • Gene symbol (TENxSymbol)
  • Ensembl gene ID (TENxEnsembl)
  • Chromosome (TENxChr)
  • Genomic start and end positions (TENxStart, TENxEnd)

These annotations are matched using a reference file containing information on duplicated gene features (features_duplicates.tsv). This mapping enables downstream integration with genomic coordinates and facilitates better interpretation of differentially expressed genes.

Code 
feat <- read.table("~/Downloads/multiome_data/reference/features_duplicates.tsv", sep="\t", header=TRUE)
rn <- rownames(rowData(multiomes3)) 
idx <- which(rn %in% feat$symbol)
idx1 <- which(feat$symbol %in% rn)
rowData(multiomes3)$TENxSymbol[idx] <- feat$symbol[idx1]
rowData(multiomes3)$TENxEnsembl[idx] <- feat$ensembl[idx1]
rowData(multiomes3)$TENxChr[idx] <- feat$chr[idx1]
rowData(multiomes3)$TENxStart[idx] <- feat$start[idx1]
rowData(multiomes3)$TENxEnd[idx] <- feat$end[idx1]

Dimensionality Reduction for Each Cell Type

In this section, we explore the variation between experimental conditions (HC and SD) at the single cell type level.

  • We loop through each cell type (label) in the multiomes3 dataset.
  • For each subset (corresponding to one label), we perform dimensionality reduction using both MDS and PCA.
  • The resulting plots are colored by experimental condition and shaped by replicate.
  • We generate side-by-side plots of the two reductions (MDS and PCA) for each label, with a common legend and a title showing the cell type name.

This helps visualize whether the sleep deprivation (SD) and control (HC) conditions lead to visible shifts in expression space within each cell type.

Code 
lbls <- unique(multiomes3$labels)

bnormpl <- lapply(lbls, function(l)
{
    # print(l)
    sce <- multiomes3[,multiomes3$labels %in% l]
    md <- scater::plotMDS(sce, color_by="condition", shape_by="replicate", point_alpha=1 )+theme_bw()+scale_color_manual(values=c(SD="black", HC="red"))
    pc <- plotPCA(sce, color_by="condition", shape_by="replicate", point_alpha=1 )+theme_bw()+scale_color_manual(values=c(SD="black", HC="red"))
    gg <- ggarrange(plotlist=list(md, pc), common.legend=TRUE) 
    gg <- annotate_figure(gg, top=ggpubr::text_grob(l,
                    color = "black", face = "bold", size = 14))
    return(gg)
})
names(bnormpl) <- lbls

Normalization Using Upper Quartile + RUVs (per Cell Type)

In this section, we apply normalization to each cell type using a combination of Upper Quartile (UQ) normalization and RUVs (Removal of Unwanted Variation using replicate samples). This step helps reduce technical noise and unwanted batch effects.

  • The dataset multiomes3 is split by individual cell type labels.
  • For each subset:
    • Upper Quartile normalization is applied to reduce library size effects.
    • The condition (HC or SD) is grouped to define biological replicates.
    • The RUVs function is used to estimate 3 unwanted variation factors (k = 3), using negative control genes.
    • The resulting normalized counts are saved under either "uqruvsk3" (if UQ was successful) or "ruvsk3" (if not).
    • PCA and MDS are recomputed using the normalized data.
    • The normalization method is saved in the metadata of the SingleCellExperiment.

This step ensures that downstream differential expression analysis is robust to technical variability.

Code 
lbls <- unique(multiomes3$labels)

scelist <- lapply(lbls, function(l)
{
    multiomes3[,multiomes3$labels %in% l]
})

names(scelist) <- lbls

scelist <- lapply(scelist, function(sce)
{
    # print(l)
    # sce <- multiomes3[,multiomes3$labels %in% l]
    reducedDims(sce)$MDS <- NULL
    uq <- EDASeq::betweenLaneNormalization(counts(sce), which="upper")
    grp <- makeGroups(sce$condition)
    rownames(grp) <- unique(sce$condition)

    k=3
    if ( isEmpty(which(is.na(uq), arr.ind=TRUE)) )
    {
        mat <- round(as.matrix(uq))
        norm <- "uqruvsk3"
    } else {
        mat <- round(as.matrix(counts(sce)))
        norm <- "ruvsk3"
    }
    ruvs <- RUVs(x=mat, cIdx=rownames(sce)[rowData(sce)$negctl], k=k,
                     scIdx=grp, round=TRUE)
    colData(sce) <- cbind.DataFrame(colData(sce), ruvs$W)
    assays(sce)[[norm]] <- ruvs$normalizedCounts
    sce <- runMDS(sce, assay.type=norm)
    sce <- runPCA(sce, assay.type=norm)
    
    metadata(sce)$norm <- norm
    return(sce)
})
names(scelist) <- lbls

Plot MDS and PCA after Normalization (per Cell Type)

This section visualizes the effect of normalization and the separation of samples by condition (HC vs SD) for each cell type individually.

  • For each cell type in the list scelist:
    • We extract the normalized SingleCellExperiment object.
    • We generate two dimensionality reduction plots: one using MDS and one using PCA.
    • Both plots are colored by the experimental condition and shaped by replicate, making batch effects and biological trends visually detectable.
    • The plots are arranged side-by-side using ggarrange, and a title is added that includes the cell type and the normalization method used (from metadata(sce)$norm).
  • Finally, for each cell type, the same set of plots is printed twice vertically using ggarrange with nrow=2 (may be for layout testing or optional repetition).
Code 
normpl <- lapply(seq_along(scelist), function(i)
{
    sce <- scelist[[i]]
    l <- names(scelist)[i]
    md <- scater::plotMDS(sce, color_by="condition", shape_by="replicate", point_alpha=1 )+theme_bw()+scale_color_manual(values=c(SD="black", HC="red"))
    pc <- plotPCA(sce, color_by="condition", shape_by="replicate", point_alpha=1 )+theme_bw()+scale_color_manual(values=c(SD="black", HC="red"))
    gg <- ggarrange(plotlist=list(md, pc), common.legend=TRUE)
    gg <- annotate_figure(gg, top=ggpubr::text_grob(
                            paste0(l, " ", metadata(sce)$norm),
                            color="black", face="bold", size=14))
    return(gg)
})

names(normpl) <- names(scelist)
for (l in lbls)
{
    print(ggarrange(plotlist=list(normpl[[l]], normpl[[l]]), nrow=2))
}

Run Differential Expression with UQ+RUVsK3 Normalization

In this step, we perform differential gene expression (DGE) analysis for each cell type using the edgeR framework, incorporating normalization from the previous RUVs (Removing Unwanted Variation) step.

  • Iterates over each normalized SingleCellExperiment in scelist.
  • Constructs a DGEList object from raw counts and associated metadata.
  • If the sample was normalized with Upper Quartile + RUVs (uqruvsk3), it computes offsets using library size and normalization factors to account for sequencing depth.
  • Filters lowly expressed genes using filterByExpr(), requiring at least 5 counts across conditions.
  • Calls a custom applyEdgeR() function, applying the contrast "SD - HC" and including the RUV W factors (W_1, W_2, W_3) as covariates.
  • Reorders and integrates the differential results into the rowData() of the original object.
  • Flags significantly differentially expressed genes (FDR < 0.05) with a sign column.
  • (Commented out) An optional block to save the resulting DEG tables for each cell type as .tsv
Code 
scelist <- lapply(scelist, function(sce)
{
    y <- DGEList(counts(sce), samples=colData(sce))
    if (metadata(sce)$norm=="uqruvsk3")
    {
        y1 <- calcNormFactors(y, method="upperquartile")
        offs <- log(y1$samples$lib.size*y1$samples$norm.factors)
    } else {
        offs <- NULL
    }
    
    keep <- filterByExpr(y, group=sce$condition, min.count=5, min.total.count=0)
    keep.genes <- data.frame(keep[keep=="TRUE"])
    sce <- sce[rownames(keep.genes),]
    
    cntrs <- c("SD - HC")
    res <- applyEdgeR(counts=counts(sce), colData=colData(sce),
                          factors="condition", wnames=c("W_1", "W_2", "W_3"),
                          contrasts=cntrs, p.threshold=1,
                          edgeroffs=offs)[[1]]
    
    res <- res[order(match(rownames(res),rownames(sce))),]
    rowData(sce) <- rowData(sce)[,-2]
    rowData(sce) <- cbind.DataFrame(rowData(sce), res)
    rowData(sce)$sign <- rowData(sce)$FDR < 0.05
    return(sce)
})

Compare DEGs and Nuclei Count

This section explores the relationship between the number of nuclei (cells) detected per cell type and the number of differentially expressed genes (DEGs) identified. This is done in two parts: using all cell types, and then filtering to those with more than 100 nuclei to reduce noise from low-abundance populations.

Compare DEGs and Nuclei Count (All Cell Types)

For each cell type: - The function statDEG() summarizes DEG statistics, likely counting the number of significant genes. - These summaries are collected into a combined table with buildTab(), which returns a data.frame containing at least:
- the number of nuclei (Nuclei),
- the number of DEGs (DEGs),
- and the label (Label) for each cell type. - A scatter plot is created: - X-axis: log-transformed number of nuclei. - Y-axis: log-transformed number of DEGs. - Labels are annotated using geom_text_repel() for readability. - A quadratic regression line is fitted (y ~ poly(x, 2)) to highlight any non-linear trends. - The results are visualized both as a ggplot and as an interactive data table using DT::datatable().

Code 
scelist <- lapply(scelist, function(sce)
{
    statDEG(sce)
})

tab <- buildTab(scelist)
# tab$Genotype <- "Shank3"
# writexl::write_xlsx(tab, path="~/Downloads/multiome_data/results/Supplementary_Table_3_S3.xlsx")
# neurlbl <- c("CA1", "CA1-do","CA1-ProS", "CA2", "CA3", "SUB-ProS", "DG","Lamp5", "Sncg", "Vip", "Serpinf1",
#                                           "Ntng1", "Pvalb", "Sst", "Sst-Chodl")

# tab <- tab[rownames(tab) %in% neurlbl,]
# tab<-tab[-which(tab$Nuclei<100),]
# Scatter plot of log(nuclei) vs log(DEGs)
p1 <- ggplot(tab, aes(x = log(Nuclei), y = log(DEGs), color=Label)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  #scale_color_manual(values = neuronal_color) + 
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text = element_text(size = 7), 
        axis.title = element_text(size = 7)) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, 2), se = FALSE, col = "grey") +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = Label), size = 3,
                   box.padding   = 0.35) +
  ggtitle("S3")
  # geom_label_repel(aes(label = Label), size = 2,
  #                  box.padding   = 0.1,
  #                  point.padding = 0,
  #                  segment.color = "grey50")+scale_color_manual(values=palette)
datatable(tab)

Compare DEGs and Nuclei (Filtered: >100 Nuclei)

This analysis filters out low-abundance cell types, retaining only those with more than 100 detected nuclei. This threshold helps focus on well-sampled populations, where differential expression analysis is statistically more reliable.

  • A subset tab1 is created from the original summary table tab, keeping only cell types with more than 100 nuclei.
  • A scatter plot is generated to show the relationship between the log-transformed number of nuclei and log-transformed number of DEGs.
  • Labels for each point represent the cell type (Label), with overlap prevented using geom_text_repel.
  • A polynomial trend line (y ~ poly(x, 2)) is added to model the relationship.
  • The corresponding data is displayed in an interactive table using DT::datatable
Code 
tab <- tab[tab$Nuclei>100,]
p1 <- ggplot(tab, aes(x = log(Nuclei), y = log(DEGs), color=Label)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  #scale_color_manual(values = neuronal_color) + 
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text = element_text(size = 7), 
        axis.title = element_text(size = 7)) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, 2), se = FALSE, col = "grey") +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = Label), size = 3,
                   box.padding   = 0.35) +
  ggtitle("S3 100 Nuclei")
  # geom_label_repel(aes(label = Label), size = 2,
  #                  box.padding   = 0.1,
  #                  point.padding = 0,
  #                  segment.color = "grey50") + scale_color_manual(values=palette) 
datatable(tab)

Compare DEGs vs Nuclei in Neuronal Types (>100 Nuclei)

This analysis focuses specifically on neuronal populations that are well-sampled (i.e., having more than 100 nuclei). By excluding non-neuronal cells, the relationship between sample size and DEG count is analyzed within a more functionally homogeneous group.

Steps performed: - Filter tab to retain only rows where the number of nuclei exceeds 100. - Further subset to include only neuronal cell types, based on the superclass annotation in the original multiome dataset. - Create a scatter plot showing the log-transformed number of nuclei vs. log-transformed number of DEGs. - Annotate cell types with geom_text_repel for clarity. - Add a quadratic regression line to highlight overall trends. - Present results both graphically and as an interactive table.

Code 
tab2 <- tab[tab$Nuclei>100,]
neuronallabels <- unique(multiomes3$label[multiomes3$superclass != "Non Neuronal"])
tab2<-tab2[tab2$Label %in% neuronallabels,]
p1 <- ggplot(tab2, aes(x = log(Nuclei), y = log(DEGs), color=Label)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  #scale_color_manual(values = neuronal_color) + 
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none", axis.text = element_text(size = 7), 
        axis.title = element_text(size = 7)) +
  stat_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ poly(x, 2), se = FALSE, col = "grey") +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = Label), size = 3,
                   box.padding   = 0.35)+#,
#                   point.padding = 0)+#,
                   #segment.color = "grey50") + #scale_color_manual(values=palette) +
  # geom_label_repel(aes(label = Label), size = 2,
  #                  box.padding   = 0.1,
  #                  point.padding = 0,
  #                  segment.color = "grey50") + scale_color_manual(values=palette) +
    ggtitle("S3 100 nuclei neuronal")
datatable(tab2)

MDS Plots of Superclasses

This section explores differences in gene expression between broad neuronal classes — GABAergic, Glutamatergic, and Non-Neuronal — in wild-type samples. It involves the following steps:

  • Load the pseudobulk multiome dataset.
  • Define three main cell-type superclasses.
  • Load and annotate both negative and positive control genes used for normalization.
  • Filter out low-represented cell types (fewer than 6 replicates).
  • Normalize each subclass and compute MDS (Multidimensional Scaling).
  • Generate separate MDS plots for each superclass subset.
Code

Session Info
